name: Bibliographical Society Major/Minor Grants
amount_or_value: up to GBP 2,000 (Pantzer Fellowship up to GBP 4,000)
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: yes -- "The Society particularly supports those who have no opportunity of gaining institutional support for their research"
residency_or_citizenship_limits: none stated for UK applicants; up to GBP 1,000 extra travel funding at the Society's discretion for applicants from outside UK/Europe "where no other funding is available"
deadline_or_rolling: annual round, see bibsoc.org.uk guidelines (check current cycle)
what_it_funds: bibliographical/book-history research: archive visits, photography, copies, travel
fit_1to5: 5 -- explicitly for researchers without institutional support; funds the exact costs (copies, images, archive visits) this project incurs

name: Hugging Face Community GPU Grants
amount_or_value: in-kind ZeroGPU or A10G hardware inside a Hugging Face Space (no fixed cash value quoted)
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: yes -- eligible projects include "academic research demos, open-source projects with traction, and other useful machine learning projects"; no institutional affiliation required
deadline_or_rolling: rolling, applied for from the Space's own hardware settings page, no external portal
what_it_funds: GPU compute for a public demo/tool (e.g. a hosted homophonic-cipher solver or key-decoder Space)
fit_1to5: 4 -- free, no affiliation gate, but only funds a public-facing HF Space, not the project's private research compute (Claude API usage)

name: Lambda Cloud Research Grant
amount_or_value: up to $5,000 GPU cloud credits
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: unclear -- described as open to "qualifying AI and machine learning researchers and research groups"; no explicit institutional-affiliation requirement found in the sources read, but not confirmed on Lambda's own application page (competitive, application-based)
what_it_funds: GPU cloud instances for training/fine-tuning AI/ML work
fit_1to5: 4 -- sizeable in-kind GPU credit, no affiliation gate found, but the project's actual bottleneck is Claude API usage, not raw GPU training, so credits would mostly go unused

name: JPASS (individual JSTOR access)
amount_or_value: $19.50/month or $199/year (10 article downloads/month, unlimited online reading)
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: yes -- "designed for people doing research without access to JSTOR through a school or library"
what_it_funds: JSTOR journal access for the scholarship pass of the verifier brief
fit_1to5: 4 -- guaranteed, no-affiliation JSTOR access at modest personal cost; a paid fallback if the existing JSTOR_USER/JSTOR_PASS credential (CLAUDE.md) ever lapses

name: Folger Institute Short-Term Fellowships
amount_or_value: $5,000/month in residence, $4,000/month virtual, 1-3 months
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: yes -- "open to college and university faculty, independent scholars, artists, public scholars, writers... and other knowledge holders"
residency_or_citizenship_limits: none found stated; virtual option available
deadline_or_rolling: annual cycle, see folger.edu for current dates
what_it_funds: research residency drawing on Folger's British/European manuscript and print collection, 15th-18th century
fit_1to5: 4 -- explicitly welcomes independent scholars and a virtual track, and the collection period overlaps several project targets (English 16th-18th c. ciphers), but needs a Folger-specific target identified first

name: National Coalition of Independent Scholars (NCIS) Research Grants
amount_or_value: $599 (Research Grant); $250 (Conference Support Grant, 3x/year); Elizabeth Eisenstein Prize $350
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: yes, but membership-gated -- "available ONLY to fully vetted and paid-up members of NCIS", requiring "a full member... for a minimum of 15 consecutive months prior to the relevant grant application deadline"
residency_or_citizenship_limits: none found stated (US-founded but international membership)
deadline_or_rolling: 3 cycles per year once a member
what_it_funds: independent scholars' research costs generally
fit_1to5: 4 -- exactly the target population (independent, unaffiliated scholars) but the 15-month membership seasoning means no near-term money; worth joining now for next year

name: Anthropic External Researcher Access Program
amount_or_value: $1,000 in Claude API credits ("for rare special cases, we may approve a higher quantity")
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: unclear -- FAQ names no institutional-affiliation requirement, but restricts the topic, not the applicant: "specifically designed to support researchers working on AI safety and alignment topics we consider high priority"
deadline_or_rolling: rolling, evaluated "the first Monday of each month"
what_it_funds: Claude API usage only, for AI-safety/alignment research
fit_1to5: 3 -- no affiliation gate and directly relevant funder (more Claude usage is exactly what the project wants), but the stated scope is AI safety/alignment, not historical cryptography, so eligibility on topic is doubtful without reframing the request

name: Royal Historical Society Open Research Support Grants
amount_or_value: GBP 500 or GBP 1,000
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: no (membership-gated) -- "Applicants for Royal Historical Society funding must be members of the Society"; open to "all historians... who are not postgraduate students or early career researchers", membership itself has no institutional requirement
residency_or_citizenship_limits: none found stated beyond RHS membership
what_it_funds: archive visits, historical sites, interviews, conference attendance for historians "without access to research funding"
fit_1to5: 3 -- good fit for archive-visit costs once RHS membership (open to independents) is obtained; not free money, a subscription plus application

name: Bibliographical Society of America -- New Scholars Program
amount_or_value: not confirmed on the pages read (travel/presentation support tied to the BSA annual meeting; amount not stated in the sources read)
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: yes -- "Booksellers, librarians, curators, collectors, junior... academics, graduate students at the dissertation level, and independent scholars are all welcome to apply"
what_it_funds: presenting bibliographical research at the BSA annual meeting
fit_1to5: 3 -- explicitly open to independent scholars, but it is a presentation opportunity, not primarily a cash grant for fieldwork

name: Huntington Library Short-Term Fellowships for Non-Traditional Scholars
funder: The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens
amount_or_value: $4,000/month, 1-3 months
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: yes -- "several short-term awards are specifically designed for independent or nontraditional scholars who either trained or currently work outside of academia, many of whom will not have a Ph.D." (e.g. the Alan Jutzi Residential Fellowship for Non-Traditional Scholars)
residency_or_citizenship_limits: requires physical residency at the Huntington (San Marino, California) for the fellowship period
what_it_funds: research residency using Huntington's collections
fit_1to5: 3 -- strong independent-scholar fit and a real stipend, but only useful if a project target's material is held at the Huntington, which is not yet established

name: Newberry Library -- Arthur and Lila Weinberg Fellowship for Independent Scholars
amount_or_value: $5,000/month, 9-12 months (long-term fellowship rate)
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: yes -- "for an independent scholar or researcher who wishes to participate in the rich and varied scholarly and public programming of the Newberry"
residency_or_citizenship_limits: requires residency in Chicago for the fellowship period
what_it_funds: a long, funded residency; large stipend but a near-full-year commitment away from other work
fit_1to5: 3 -- very well-funded and explicitly for independent scholars, but the year-long residency is a large commitment relative to this project's remote, distributed way of working, and needs a Newberry-relevant target

name: Experiment.com science crowdfunding
amount_or_value: all-or-nothing crowdfunding; platform takes 8% + ~3-5% payment processing on successfully funded projects
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: yes -- open platform, no institutional affiliation required to start a project
deadline_or_rolling: rolling; campaign runs a set time frame chosen by the project
what_it_funds: whatever the campaign proposes (e.g. an archive copy-order fund)
fit_1to5: 3 -- no gatekeeping at all and the project has a genuine public-interest story (15 N4 readings), but it means naming the project publicly and running an outreach campaign, a different kind of effort than the other rows

name: British Library free Reader Pass
amount_or_value: free (in-person registration only, since a cyber-attack removed online pre-registration)
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: yes -- "Anyone aged 18 or over can use the Reading Rooms... all you need is a free Reader Pass"
residency_or_citizenship_limits: none stated, but registration is in person only, at St Pancras (London) or Boston Spa (Yorkshire)
what_it_funds: free physical access to BL manuscripts and reading rooms (not digitisation or copy costs, which are billed separately)
application_effort_hours: 1 (if already able to travel to London/Boston Spa)
fit_1to5: 3 -- free and open to anyone, but requires in-person travel to register and does not itself cover copy orders or digitisation, which remain the person's REQUEST.md items

name: Wikimedia Research Fund
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: unclear -- open to "individuals, groups, and organizations with research interests on or about Wikimedia projects", but applicants "should be established Wikimedia researchers (i.e., people with a history of conducting research related to Wikimedia projects)"
what_it_funds: research about Wikimedia projects, not general historical/cryptographic research
fit_1to5: 2 -- this project is not research about Wikimedia projects; a stretch unless framed as a study of open-knowledge contribution practices, which would misrepresent the work

name: IHR Scouloudi Historical Awards
funder: Institute of Historical Research / Scouloudi Foundation
amount_or_value: full-year and half-year fellowships, or smaller research/publication awards (amount not confirmed on the pages read)
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: no -- "Candidates must be UK citizens or graduates of UK universities with honours or postgraduate degrees in history"
residency_or_citizenship_limits: UK citizenship or a UK university degree required; one source notes the fellowship round "will not be held" in at least one recent year -- confirm current status before relying on it
deadline_or_rolling: not confirmed active for the current cycle
what_it_funds: advanced historical research intended for publication
fit_1to5: 2 -- hard nationality/degree gate and uncertain whether the award is currently running; low priority unless the owner holds a UK degree

name: Society of Antiquaries of London -- Minor Research Grants
amount_or_value: not confirmed on the pages read (described as "minor grants")
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: no -- "Minor grants are open to fellows and UK citizens who are not fellows"
what_it_funds: antiquarian/historical research and travel
fit_1to5: 2 -- UK-citizen gate; relevant to manuscript/antiquarian work in principle but excludes non-UK applicants

name: NEH Public Scholars Program
amount_or_value: not confirmed on the pages read (a stipended book-length-project award)
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: yes on affiliation -- "accepts applications from individuals, whether they have an affiliation with a scholarly institution or not... NEH encourages submissions from independent scholars" -- but gated on prior publication: "must have written and published a nonfiction book with a university press or trade press; OR... at least three nonfiction articles or essays in general-interest publications"
residency_or_citizenship_limits: US citizens, and foreign nationals resident in the US or its jurisdictions for the 3 years before the deadline
deadline_or_rolling: 22 April 2026 for the 2026 round (already past); 2026 competition restricted to "American history and culture and Western civilization" topics only
what_it_funds: a book-length work of humanities scholarship for a general audience
fit_1to5: 2 -- no affiliation gate, but the project's readings are not yet a publishable book and the owner has no qualifying prior publication on file here; also outside this cycle's restricted topic and past its 2026 deadline

name: Anthropic AI for Science
amount_or_value: up to $20,000 in API credits over 6 months
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: no -- "researchers attached to research institutions" is the stated eligibility; independent, unaffiliated researchers are not mentioned as eligible
residency_or_citizenship_limits: none stated beyond the institutional requirement
deadline_or_rolling: rolling, evaluated "the first Monday of each month"
what_it_funds: Claude API access (standard models only) for high-impact scientific research
fit_1to5: 2 -- by far the largest credit amount found and a strong topical fit (more Claude usage), but blocked on the explicit institutional-affiliation requirement; the strongest case in this list for the affiliation-unlocks-it note below

name: OpenAI Researcher Access Program
amount_or_value: up to $1,000 in API credits, valid 12 months
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: no -- "Researcher(s) with an active affiliation to an academic institution or other research organization, as well as nonprofits conducting research activities" are eligible; independents without such affiliation are not
residency_or_citizenship_limits: "applicants must be based in countries supported by our API"
what_it_funds: OpenAI API usage for responsible-AI-deployment research
fit_1to5: 2 -- affiliation-gated, and the project is built on Claude, not OpenAI models, so the fit is weak even if eligible

name: Google Cloud Research Credits
amount_or_value: up to $5,000 (faculty/postdoc/nonprofit-lab researcher) or $1,000 (PhD student)
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: no -- "Applicants must be faculty, PhD students, or postdoctoral researchers at regionally accredited academic institutions or nonprofit research institutions"
residency_or_citizenship_limits: none found stated beyond the institutional requirement
what_it_funds: Google Cloud compute for a research proposal
fit_1to5: 2 -- clean institutional gate excludes an unaffiliated individual outright; would need a nonprofit-lab wrapper to qualify

name: AWS Cloud Credit for Research
amount_or_value: student awards capped at $5,000; faculty/staff awards uncapped
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: no -- "Researchers at accredited research institutions can apply, defined as full-time faculty, full-time research staff, or graduate, post-graduate or PhD students enrolled at an accredited research institution"
what_it_funds: AWS compute for a cloud-hosted proof-of-concept, tool, or data migration
fit_1to5: 2 -- institutional gate excludes an unaffiliated individual; the project also runs on Claude/local tooling rather than AWS-hosted infrastructure

name: BnF Pass Recherche (reader card)
amount_or_value: paid (1-day, 5-day or annual unlimited rate; exact tariff not confirmed on the pages read); reduced rate for under-25s/students under 35
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: yes in principle -- open registration via inscriptionbilletterie.bnf.fr, with a consultation interview to set the pass duration; no institutional affiliation required for the standard researcher pass
what_it_funds: physical/onsite access to BnF's research reading rooms (manuscripts already reached online via Gallica IIIF do not need this)
fit_1to5: 2 -- useful mainly if a target ever needs an onsite BnF consultation beyond what Gallica's IIIF API already serves (which is most current use); low priority while the API route works

name: Modal for Academics
amount_or_value: reported up to $10,000-25,000 historically; program described as currently paused
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: no -- "available to university faculty, postdocs, PhD students, and course instructors at accredited institutions"; secondary sources say the academic grant tier is currently paused with a waitlist
residency_or_citizenship_limits: none found stated beyond the institutional requirement
deadline_or_rolling: waitlist only (paused) as of the pages read
what_it_funds: serverless GPU compute
fit_1to5: 1 -- institutional gate plus reportedly paused; not actionable now

name: Microsoft Accelerate Foundation Models Research (AFMR)
amount_or_value: previously up to $20,000 in Azure credits
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: not applicable -- "The Accelerating Foundation Models Research program has reached its conclusion"
what_it_funds: was Azure OpenAI / foundation-model access for academic research
fit_1to5: 1 -- program concluded; listed only because the brief named it and to record that it is no longer open

name: Google for Startups Cloud Program
amount_or_value: startup-tier cloud credits (varies by program stage)
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: no -- requires registering as a startup company (funded or pre-seed with a registered entity), not an individual research project
what_it_funds: Google Cloud usage for an incorporated startup
fit_1to5: 1 -- this project is not a company and has no plan to become one; included only because the brief named it

name: American Cryptogram Association
amount_or_value: none found
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: not applicable -- no grant, scholarship, or research-funding program was found on the ACA's own site or in search results; it is a hobbyist cipher-solving membership organisation (newsletter, tools, word lists)
what_it_funds: n/a
fit_1to5: 1 -- no funding program exists to apply to; worth membership only for the community/word-list resources, not money

name: Sloan Foundation Open Source in Science
amount_or_value: not stated for individual projects
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: no in practice -- the program states it does not fund "individual open source development projects" but rather "tooling, institutions, economic models, and incentives" at an ecosystem level; a two-page letter of inquiry is the entry point
what_it_funds: ecosystem-level open-source-in-research infrastructure, not a single project's compute or archive costs
fit_1to5: 1 -- explicitly not the kind of individual-project grant this work needs

name: Mozilla Technology Fund / Fellowship
amount_or_value: MOSS/Technology Fund up to $50,000 for open-source teams; Fellowship is a stipended placement
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: unclear/closed -- "MOSS applications are currently closed... appears to be on indefinite hiatus"; the 2026 Fellowship nomination process is nomination-only and "now closed"
what_it_funds: public-interest open-source software projects, or a fellow's own project during a placement
fit_1to5: 1 -- both routes are closed or nomination-only right now; revisit if MOSS reopens

name: Gale State Papers Online -- individual access
amount_or_value: institutional subscription only; one source cites roughly GBP 300,000 for a university-wide licence, no individual price found
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: no -- sold only as an institutional subscription; "State Papers Online packages are simply unaffordable for many institutions"; no individual-researcher purchase route was found
what_it_funds: n/a -- not purchasable by an individual
fit_1to5: 1 -- confirms this route needs an institutional partner (e.g. a library that already subscribes) rather than a grant; see README partnership note

name: DECRYPT project / HistoCrypt community
funder: Swedish Research Council (DECRYPT, 2019-2024, concluded) / HistoCrypt conference series
amount_or_value: no direct funding found; DECRYPT itself already ended and was never open to outside applicants
open_to_individuals_without_affiliation: not applicable as a funding source -- DECRYPT was a closed academic grant (2018-06074) already concluded; HistoCrypt is a conference and community (the DECODE database this project already uses), not a grant body
what_it_funds: n/a for funding; the value here is the DECODE database and the HistoCrypt community/citation network this project already draws on
fit_1to5: 1 -- not a funding route; listed to record that none was found, and that the practical value (DECODE, citations) is already being used per CLAUDE.md's outreach rules
